description: Who I am: A passionate developer and innovator participating in Hackathon Gravity, driven by the goal of building impactful tech solutions that improve everyday lives.
summary:
During deep-space missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays of up to 20 minutes make real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. Astronauts must have complete medical autonomy. 

To solve this challenge, we developed ASTRA (Astronaut Safety Tracking & Real-time Analytics) — an offline-first, mission-critical health dashboard designed for long-duration spaceflight. ASTRA tracks 8 essential biometric and behavioral telemetry indicators (including blood pressure, heart rate, SpO2, sleep duration, and hydration) linked to the 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight defined by the NASA Human Research Program (HRP).

The platform features an interactive 3D astronaut digital twin, real-time Chart.js physiological trend analytics, autonomous emergency diagnostic alerts (such as microgravity hypotension and SANS risk detection), and guided clinical countermeasures. To combat mission-induced cognitive fatigue and sensory-vestibular discordance, ASTRA also integrates a gamified 3D neuro-cognitive flight simulation for non-invasive stress de-escalation.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

ASTRA is an autonomous health management platform tailored for exploration-class spaceflight:

  • Daily Biometric Check-in: Astronauts rapidly record vitals (Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, Core Temperature, Blood Glucose, SpO2, Sleep Hours, Mood, Hydration) with an intuitive stepper interface that awards daily mission XP and maintains habit streaks.
  • Autonomous Clinical Issue Alerts: When vitals enter caution or critical zones (e.g., blood pressure < 85 mmHg due to cephalad fluid shift, or SpO2 <= 90%), ASTRA triggers high-visibility HUD emergency alert banners with clinical diagnostic explanations and step-by-step countermeasure protocols.
  • Interactive 3D Physiological Digital Twin: A WebGL/Three.js 3D astronaut model visualizes organ-level impacts across 7 physiological systems (Cardiovascular, Respiratory, Neurological, Metabolic, Immune, Musculoskeletal, and Behavioral).
  • Chart.js Historical Telemetry: Multi-day historical graphs with normal physiological threshold bands, moving averages, and Sol-time hover diagnostics.
  • Stress Relief Combat Therapy: A high-speed 3D flight simulation targeting vestibular-ocular recalibration and acute cortisol reduction through flow-state pursuit mechanics.

2. What benefits and impact does it have?

  • Medical Autonomy: Enables crews to independently diagnose and mitigate health threats during communication blackouts.
  • Early Intervention: Prevents acute escalation of spaceflight-specific conditions like orthostatic intolerance, Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), and dehydration-induced renal calculi.
  • Cognitive Resilience: Combines gamification mechanics (ranks, badges, XP) and neuro-sensory flight decompression to combat astronaut isolation and mission burnout.

3. Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend Core: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS 4.
  • 3D Graphics & Shaders: Three.js (r187), GLTF Loader, UnrealBloomPass post-processing shaders, ACESFilmic tone mapping.
  • Data Visualization: Chart.js, react-chartjs-2.
  • Animations: Framer Motion.
  • Data & Persistence: Supabase real-time database with offline-first LocalStorage fallback and PWA Service Workers.
  • Deployment: Vercel with automated continuous deployment.

4. Spaceflight Factors Considered

  • Microgravity Fluid Redistribution: Cephalad venous engorgement causing lower-limb hypotension and intracranial pressure spikes.
  • Blunted Thirst Reflex: Decreased hydration perception in microgravity compounded by calcium bone resorption.
  • Circadian & Sleep Disruption: Spacecraft noise and 90-minute orbital light-dark cycles causing chronic sleep debt.
  • Sensory-Vestibular Discordance: Space Motion Sickness (SMS) during initial adaptation and re-adaptation.
